A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DANG noise framework and DA-GNN method. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification and link-prediction experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and training-time measurements in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original PolitiFact statistical analysis, noise-generation controls, and expanded sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.2.1 replaces v1's Bernoulli-sampled adjacency description with probability-weighted adjacency. However, v1 already describes probability weights on a proxy graph in Appendix B and Algorithm 1, which remain unchanged. The PDFs do not resolve whether inference changed or its description was clarified; the encoders, decoders, and losses are retained.

E1.justification: The seven prediction benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 adds PolitiFact fake-versus-benign news analysis in Appendix C.1 and tests additional corruption scenarios with noise dependencies or independent structural noise absent. The added Computers sensitivity analysis uses an existing dataset.

E2.justification: The main-table comparators are unchanged, but Figure 4 expands the Cora comparisons: feature noise adds RSGNN, STABLE, NRGNN, and RTGNN; structure noise adds AirGNN, NRGNN, and RTGNN; label noise adds AirGNN, RSGNN, STABLE, and SG-GSR. Newly cited label-noise methods are not shown as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design through approximately fourfold dependency-induced corruption, removal or doubling of independent structural noise, and separate doubling of fraudster numbers and activity. PolitiFact introduces BERT-based topic clustering and neighborhood-entropy analysis. These are additional protocols; the original splits, prediction metrics, and main-experiment hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3 adds systematic tests of whether robustness depends on synthetic and e-commerce noise-generation choices. Sensitivity analysis adds k and extends to Computers, while Appendix C.1 adds a real-data case study. Existing causal ablations and qualitative analyses are retained. Zero-weight points disappear from the sensitivity plots despite remaining discussed.

E5.justification: v2 adds quartiles and a Mann–Whitney U test for PolitiFact entropy, plus Mann–Whitney tests for both previously qualitative clean/noisy distributions in Appendix F.4. It explains numerical underflow behind reported zero p-values. Both versions retain the same three-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, training times, and combination-method results are numerically unchanged. v2 adds substantial results in Tables 4 and 8–12 and expanded comparison/sensitivity plots. New settings show mixed rankings: Table 12 reports DA-GNN at 55.6±1.0 versus STABLE at 58.1±2.0 on Auto with doubled structure noise. These are additional-setting results, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 4.2.1 and Appendix B remove the explicit Bernoulli definitions of the sampled latent and prior adjacency matrices, replacing them with probability weights and a qualitative similarity prior. The ELBO derivation, conditional-independence assumptions, and computational-complexity reasoning otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction removes two explicit first-of-kind assertions concerning examination of the practical noise-assumption gap and provision of realistic-noise benchmarks. The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: DANG, DA-GNN, new benchmarks, and broad noise robustness.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds concrete applicability exceptions involving fixed molecular and protein-interaction structures. The sensitivity discussion now acknowledges that k requires tuning and explains its importance. Appendix C.1 interprets news-entropy differences as evidence of noise propagation. The earlier limitation concerning reverse structure-to-feature effects is retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents BERT embeddings, k-means topic assignment, and neighborhood entropy for the new PolitiFact analysis, and names SciPy when explaining significance calculations. Existing model dimensions, tuning ranges, early-learning duration, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The label-noise discussion adds TSS, pairwise-interaction learning, ERASE, GNN Cleaner, and Divide and Denoise; DECOR is cited for PolitiFact. Conversely, v1's Appendix D comparisons with GraphDE and RGIB and their references are removed. The central positioning around dependent graph noise remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Local revisions shorten introductory examples and contribution statements, clarify model exposition, introduce formulation/discussion subsections, and reorder experimental appendices. Detailed qualitative analysis moves from the main text to Appendix F.4, and acknowledgements replace the generic impact statement.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout with extensively repositioned displays. v2 adds six tables, expands Figure 4's curves and legends, and adds sensitivity panels and a Computers figure. The qualitative distribution figure moves from main-text Figure 7 to appendix Figure 13.

improvement.justification: The added generator controls, broader Figure 4 comparisons, and explicit tuning/applicability qualifications strengthen the paper's empirical support. The gain is limited by interpretation problems: PolitiFact entropy associations do not establish causal noise propagation, and Section 5.5's consistent-superiority claim conflicts with exceptions in the new tables, including Table 12. The revision provides useful additional validation without fully aligning its conclusions with that evidence.
